sources.paper_title: Temporal cascade of frontal, motor and muscle processes underlying human action-stopping
sources.author: Sumitash Jana, Ricci Hannah ... Adam R Aron

copyright.statement: This article is distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use and redistribution provided that the original author and source are credited.

sources.title: Hypothetical model of the temporal cascade of processes underlying human action-stopping.
sources.legend: Following the Go signal, after a delay, the thalamocortical drive starts building up. After a while this drive is sufficient to activate muscles via the corticospinal pathways. Following the Stop signal, the right PFC including the rIFC and the preSMA gets activated at ~ 120 ms. These region/s activate (green connections) the STN of the basal ganglia which in turn activates the globus pallidus interna which via its inhibition (red connection) on the motor regions of the thalamus cuts down the ‘drive’ of the motor cortex. This results in a global motor suppression at ~ 140 ms after the Stop signal. This suppression is reflected in the hand muscle at ~ 160 ms which is measured as the CancelTime. There is a delay of ~ 60 ms at the muscle level which gets added to the behavioral estimate of SSRT.
sources.credit: Sumitash Jana; Ricci Hannah; Vignesh Muralidharan; Adam R Aron
sources.full_reference: Sumitash Jana; Ricci Hannah; Vignesh Muralidharan; Adam R Aron (2020). Temporal cascade of frontal, motor and muscle processes underlying human action-stopping. https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.50371

These components provide more specific targets for measurement than a broad judgment about a person's character.

sources.caption: Clinical demonstration: a skilled-action error. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
sources.teaching_note: This separate teaching case is not evidence of CTE or a finding in a former player. It demonstrates why a clinical record preserves successful responses alongside errors. Comparing comprehension, voluntary movement, and action organization helps identify whether an apparent failure reflects language, motor ability, or the production of a learned skilled action.

sources.teaching_note: Football also requires anticipating possible paths while monitoring a changing environment, but this experiment did not test players or diagnose injury. It provides a concrete cognitive-neuroscience method: specify the goal, control the information, and measure the actions used to plan. Clinical evaluation can then ask which component of performance has changed for a particular person.
